- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts show gradual upward drift, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70.00), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast growth to +0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model underestimates downside risk — adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and event balance is bearish, model often fails to reflect volatility — add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- If model shows steady upward trend over 30d but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 70s → 68s), reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 10d.  
- For auctions with high supply net (e.g., >10 events/30d), model tends to overreact — apply 1–2% downward correction to forecast mean.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model often ignores risk — apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast.  
- When bullish sentiment is high but supply net is negative, model overestimates upside — reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect supply constraint.
